payload.headline: Trial-to-paid conversion fell in workspaces with 11+ people after the 2026-02-10 billing-screen release; activation and the upstream funnel are flat

cause.does_not_prove: That s51_plus alone is material. It is grouped with s11_50 because it moved the same way by a similar amount. Tickets carry no company_size, so they cannot be tied to the segment.
cause.text: Trial-to-paid conversion for workspaces with 11+ people (s11_50 and s51_plus) fell from 0.1244 to 0.0808 (p=0.000073). Sizes 2-10 and solo did not move materially.

cause.does_not_prove: That the release caused the drop. No experiment or rollback has tested it.

evidence.quote: The trial-end billing screen now shows one price per seat per month by default. The annual-billing toggle moved below the fold and no longer shows the savings amount.

cause.text: Release rel_0501 (2026-02-10) changed the trial-end billing screen so that annual billing is de-emphasised. Its onset matches the start of the recent period.

cause.does_not_prove: Calendar connect and first meeting were checked only by single-dimension splits, not in the combined segment. None was material.
cause.text: The loss is at trial-to-paid, after activation. Activation in the same segment is flat: 0.4521 before, 0.4512 after (p=0.945564), so no earlier funnel step moved the same way.

cause.does_not_prove: That these accounts are in the 11+ segment, or that non-converters who did not write in felt the same.

evidence.quote: Honestly the checkout page made it look more expensive than it is. We assumed monthly was the only option and that was too much for now.
I almost signed up but the pricing page at checkout just showed one number, no mention of paying yearly for less.

cause.text: Customers describe the checkout price display. 13 distinct workspaces wrote in after the onset.

payload.cheapest_test: A/B test restoring the annual toggle and savings amount on the trial-end billing screen for 11+ workspaces. It avoids rolling back the whole release. A person must approve it, because I am in prepare-only mode.
payload.question: Has anything material changed in the business over the last few weeks, and if so why?
payload.recommendation: Prepare an experiment that restores the annual-billing default and savings display for 11+ workspaces. Do not roll back the whole release yet. The sizing tool's weekly figure works through the activation gap, and activation did not move here, so it probably understates the loss.

params.test: Show the annual toggle and savings amount by default on the trial-end billing screen for a share of 11+ workspaces and compare trial_to_paid_rate with the current screen.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: That nothing else changed at trial end, such as pricing, seat counts or sales touches. No tool shows any.
ruled_out.text: Alternative: an activation or onboarding regression. Overall activation was flat (0.4011 before, 0.4015 after, p=0.950553), and in the affected segment it was flat too.

size.method: activation gap x conversion gap (activated vs not) x trials per week in the segment x ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Whether ticket authors are in the 11+ segment.
The true revenue impact. The tool's method does not fit a drop that happens after activation.
Whether s51_plus is truly affected. Its own p-value is 0.047616.
The state of any feature flag for rel_0501. The flag_state tool was denied and the release lists no flag.
Overall trial_to_paid_rate is not significant on its own (p=0.089815).
would_change_if: The experiment shows no lift in trial_to_paid_rate from restoring the annual toggle.
The ticket authors turn out to be mostly in solo or 2-10 workspaces.
Trial-to-paid recovers as the immature recent cohorts mature.

payload.hypothesis: Restoring the annual-pricing prompt at checkout for s11_50 and s51_plus brings their trial-to-paid rate back toward baseline.
payload.kill_trigger: trial_to_paid_rate for s11_50 not within 2 points of its pre-onset level for cohorts starting after the fix
